concept_summary: A bar at 1237 Polk St in the Polk Street NCD adding live entertainment and amplified sound to its existing operation, with limited food service, closing after midnight but before 2 a.m.

overall.line: Of the 5 approvals this concept needs: 2 further review (zoning and use, entertainment permit), 2 insufficient information (alcohol licence, building permit and change of use), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning to authorize intensification of the existing bar use by adding entertainment, and confirm in the intake meeting whether the 2008 CUA conditions remain operative or require amendment.

findings.text: An active ABC Type 48 license (on-sale general, public premises) is on file at 1237 Polk St, issued June 25, 2008, under the business name McTeague's Saloon.

The bar use at this address was authorized by Conditional Use Authorization case 2007.1281C, approved by the Planning Commission on March 13, 2008 (Motion #17569), under Sections 303, 723.41 and 790.22 for a bar in the Polk NCD.

findings.text: In NCD-POLK zoning, a bar on the first story is a conditional use under Planning Code Section 723, and a conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use per Section 178.
findings.verification_note: The records show a CU was approved for a bar but do not state the rules in Sections 723 or 178.

findings.text: Seven Conditional Use Authorizations for bars or entertainment in NCD-POLK within 150 meters over the last 30 years show all were approved (4 straightforward approvals, 3 with conditions), with zero denials in the candidate set.

approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

referral_steps.text: Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(1); § 1060.5(a)).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Planning Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(2)).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Department of Building Inspection for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(3)).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Department of Public Health for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(4)).
Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Fire Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(5)).

Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2.2(b)).

Revocation due to Viola tion of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. Operation (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. In addition, the operator shall be responsible for dai l y monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance wit h Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulat ed for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed -source equipment noise sha ll not exceed the decibel level s specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passer sby , appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from publ i c view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contai n ed and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Departmen t of Public Works. Works at 628.271.2000, www.sfpublicworks.org (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, an d telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)

Notices Posted at Bars and Entertainment Venues: Notices urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood in a quiet, peaceful, and orderly fashion and to not litter or block dri veways in the neighborhood, shall be well-lit and prominently displayed at all entrances to and exits from the establishment. (standard)

Lighting: All Project lighting shall be directed onto the Project site and immediately surrounding sidewalk area only, and designed and managed so as not to be a nuisance to adjac ent residents. Nighttime lighting shall be the minimum necessary to ensure safety, but shall in no case be directed so as to constitute a nuisance to any surrounding property. (standard)
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar/restaurant at 1131 Polk (102 m away, same NCD-POLK district) adding nighttime entertainment use via CUA. Filed 2019, decided April 2021 with approval and conditions—most recent use decision for entertainment intensification on this corridor.

Also required community liaison, patron behavior notices at exits, and sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral for Place of Entertainment permit at 1160 Polk (118 m, NCD-POLK) in conjunction with existing bar use, decided December 2018. Although this is a referral (not a full Commission hearing), it shows Planning's approval stance for POE permits.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning Department recommended approval of a Place of Entertainment permit to add entertainment to an existing bar, citing that entertainment is conditionally permitted in Polk NCD per prior Motion 16697. This referral suggests the pathway is routine for bars adding entertainment.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: This is the subject property's own 2008 CUA (Motion #17569) that authorized the bar use at 1237-1239 Polk under which the Type 48 license was issued. Filed November 2007, approved March 2008.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for 'Other Entertainment' at An Sibin bar, 1214 Polk (71 m, NCD-POLK), approved January 2001. This is the same Section 723.48 entertainment provision as the 1993 and 2003 cases.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved entertainment authorization for an existing bar under Section 723.48 in 2001, showing the pathway for entertainment overlay has been used repeatedly on Polk Street for two decades.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to expand Jackalope bar from 1092 Post into 1104 Polk (157 m, NCD-POLK), approved December 2016. Shows Commission approval of bar expansion in the same district and corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved expansion of an existing nonconforming bar in NCD-POLK in 2016. Although this is spatial expansion rather than entertainment intensification, it confirms the Commission's willingness to approve bar-use modifications on Polk Street during the recent decade.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to relocate Lush Lounge bar from 1092 Post to 1217 Polk (33 m, NCD-POLK), approved August 2009. Another bar modification approval on the same corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Commission approved relocation of an existing bar within NCD-POLK in 2009, demonstrating approval pathway for bar-use changes. No extracted conditions, suggesting straightforward approval for a bar relocation.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a copy of the 2008 CUA approval for this bar from SF Planning and review all conditions of approval to determine whether the entertainment proposal changes any condition.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request the full Motion and conditions from case 2007.1281C, approved March 13, 2008. Review with counsel whether adding entertainment is covered by that approval or requires an amendment. If any condition prohibits entertainment or limits the use to a bar without entertainment, the application must address that condition explicitly.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning under Section 303 for intensification of the existing bar by adding entertainment (Section 723.48, Nighttime Entertainment in NCD-POLK), including the acoustic study, a site plan showing the performance area, and a narrative explaini…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the bar use was approved in 2008 (case 2007.1281C). The proposal is to add live entertainment and amplified sound, closing after midnight but before 2 a.m. Emphasize that the entertainment will be contained within the existing enclosed space, soundproofing will be installed per the acoustic study, and the operator will implement a good-neighbor protocol including community liaison, patron notices at exits, and sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius. Cite the precedent of entertainment approvals at 1233 Polk (1993.422C, 1993), 1101-1127 Polk (2003.0611C, 2003), and 1131 Polk (2019-020049CUA, 2021), all approved in NCD-POLK.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses before opening to cover live entertainment and recorded music under federal copyright law.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The two catalogs do not overlap, so both are needed for a general mix of music. The annual fee is formula-based on occupancy and music use. State the bar's occupancy, the entertainment schedule (live and recorded music), and the days per week of operation. The licenses are effective immediately upon approval and are required before the first entertainment performance.

timeline_cost.notes: This timeline and cost covers the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 including CPI adjustment and any construction-related fee increase), the Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800), and the Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000) if a new permit is needed. The CUA is the critical path: the Entertainment Commission permit cannot be filed until the CUA is approved, and building permits for soundproofing cannot be issued until the CUA is effective. The ranges assume approval. If the CUA or entertainment permit is denied or must be withdrawn, no time or cost for those approvals is incurred and the project cannot proceed as described. The 8 comparable CUA decisions for bars or entertainment in NCD-POLK took 7 to 538 days from filing to approval (N=8 approved cases), with the most recent entertainment CUA (2019-020049CUA) taking 538 days (filed October 2019, approved April 2021). Alcohol license cost is not included because the description does not state what license transaction is proposed; if the existing Type 48 continues with no ABC action, there is no ABC filing cost. Building permit cost is not included because the scope of tenant improvements is not stated; typical soundproofing and performance area build-out costs $800–$15,000 in permit fees depending on construction valuation. ASCAP and BMI licenses ($600–$5,000 combined annually) are operational costs, not government fees, and are excluded here. The timeline assumes no appeals; a CUA appeal adds 30+ days after the Commission hearing.

records_summary: 1237 Polk St is an established bar (McTeague's Saloon) in the Polk Street NCD, holding an active Type 48 license since 2008 under a Conditional Use Authorization granted in 2008 (Motion #17569). The space was previously a restaurant/bar with a Type 47 license dating to 1986. The zoning pathway confirms that a bar is a conditional use on the first story in NCD-POLK, and because an active Type 48 exists at this address the space is read as a bar; the proposal to add entertainment to the existing bar is not a change of use. The block is extremely dense: 31 food/drink businesses and 21 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 16 bars in that radius. Four dated use decisions for bars, restaurants, and entertainment within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years show 1 approval and 3 approvals with conditions; no denials, but too few cases (N=4) for a meaningful approval rate.
